en.title: How can the same answers crown a different AI winner?
en.summary: "Better" always means better under one scoring rule. Keep the answers fixed, change the price of a wrong answer, and the leaderboard winner can flip.

en.title: Can satellites spot a forest fire while it is still small?
en.summary: A hot pixel from space is a clue, not a verdict. Finding small fires takes finer sensors, frequent revisits, and ruling out heat that is not fire.

en.title: Is the top model on the leaderboard the best one for you?
en.summary: A model has a profile, not a rank, and every benchmark has an expiry date. Start from the error you cannot afford, not from the famous name.

en.title: Why does Persian cost more tokens for some AI models?
en.summary: Persian text is usually shorter than its English equivalent (median 0.88 of the characters), yet tokenizers split it into 1.21 to 4.61 times as many tokens.

en.title: When they say an AI makes fewer mistakes, what are they not telling you?
en.summary: An error rate means nothing without its numerator and denominator: a model can make fewer mistakes simply by staying silent more often.

en.title: Can a single document hijack your AI assistant?
en.summary: To a language model, your instructions and a document's text arrive in one stream of words, so a document can give orders. Two defences, and what each one cannot do.

en.title: If the answer key is wrong, which AI loses?
en.summary: A wrong answer key only takes points from whoever answered correctly. Key errors are not neutral noise; they can change the winner unless the key is audited.

en.title: How does Google Maps know when you will arrive?
en.summary: An ETA is not a picture of traffic now; it is a forecast of the traffic you will meet. The key idea: every road segment listens to its neighbours.

en.title: Can negative marking make an AI more careful?
en.summary: Negative marking creates a silence line, t = k/(k+1). It only makes an AI more careful if the model actually changes its answers and its confidence is honest.

en.title: What happens when AI learns from AI-written text?
en.summary: If each generation learns only from the previous one, rare things vanish first and everything collapses towards one narrow answer. Keep human data alongside, and in our test it did not happen.

en.title: Can AI find where you are from one photo?
en.summary: Today's models often place an ordinary photo to the city, sometimes to the street, even with the metadata stripped. Hiding clues helps, but not enough.
